posterize_solver.name: Posterize Solver
posterize_solver.description:
Implement a complete solution for the Posterize problem. Read d distinct red values with their pixel counts and parameter k from stdin. Compute the minimum sum of squared errors when choosing at most k allowed integer values from [0,255].

Approach:
1. Parse input: d, k, then d lines of (r, p) pairs sorted by r.
2. Precompute cost(i, j): the minimum weighted squared error for covering sorted distinct values i..j with a single representative integer in [0,255]. For each contiguous group, compute the weighted mean, check floor and ceil, and pick the one with lower total squared error. Use prefix sums of p, p*r, and p*r^2 for O(1) cost computation per group.
3. DP: Let dp[g][i] = minimum SSE using g allowed values to cover the first i distinct red values. Base case: dp[1][i] = cost(0, i-1). Transition: dp[g][i] = min over split points m of dp[g-1][m] + cost(m, i-1). Final answer: dp[k][d].
4. Output the minimum SSE as a single integer.

Key details:
- Allowed values can be ANY integer in [0,255], not just input values.
- Optimal assignment to nearest representative always creates contiguous clusters in sorted order, so partitioning into contiguous groups is correct.
- With d ≤ 256 and k ≤ d, the DP is O(k * d^2) with O(1) cost lookups, which is very fast.
- All arithmetic uses Python native integers (no overflow concerns).
- Program reads one test case from stdin and prints one integer to stdout.

contract.name: Posterize Solver
contract.description: Implement a complete solution for the Posterize problem. Read d distinct red values with their pixel counts and parameter k from stdin. Compute the minimum sum of squared errors when choosing at most k allowed integer values from [0,255]. Uses contiguous group partitioning DP with O(1) cost lookups via prefix sums. Allowed representative values are any integer in [0,255], not restricted to input values. Single-module Python 3.10+ solution, standard library only.

functions.name: parse_input
functions.description: Read all tokens from stdin and parse the single test case. First token is d (number of distinct red values), second token is k (number of allowed posterization levels). Then d lines follow, each with two integers r and p. Returns a tuple (d, k, values) where values is a list of (r, p) tuples sorted by r in strictly increasing order.

functions.name: build_prefix_sums
functions.description: Given the sorted list of (r, p) pairs, compute three prefix sum arrays s0, s1, s2 each of length d+1. s0[i] = sum of p[0..i-1], s1[i] = sum of p[j]*r[j] for j in 0..i-1, s2[i] = sum of p[j]*r[j]^2 for j in 0..i-1. All arrays start with 0 at index 0.

inputs.name: values
inputs.description: Sorted list of (r, p) pairs. Length is d >= 1.

error_data.message: Cannot build prefix sums from an empty values list.

preconditions: values is sorted in strictly increasing order of r
all r in [0, 255] and all p >= 1
postconditions: s0, s1, s2 each have length len(values) + 1
for all m in [1, len(values)]: s0[m] == s0[m-1] + values[m-1].p
for all m in [1, len(values)]: s1[m] == s1[m-1] + values[m-1].p * values[m-1].r
for all m in [1, len(values)]: s2[m] == s2[m-1] + values[m-1].p * values[m-1].r * values[m-1].r
all elements of s0, s1, s2 are non-negative integers

functions.name: cost
functions.description: Compute the minimum weighted sum of squared errors for covering the contiguous group of distinct red values at sorted indices i..j (inclusive, 0-based) with a single representative integer in [0, 255]. The optimal representative is the weighted mean of the group's red values (weighted by pixel counts). Since the representative must be an integer, we evaluate floor(mean) and ceil(mean), clamp each to [0, 255], and return the smaller total SSE. The SSE for representative v over indices i..j is: sum_{m=i}^{j} p[m] * (r[m] - v)^2 = (s2[j+1]-s2[i]) - 2*v*(s1[j+1]-s1[i]) + v^2*(s0[j+1]-s0[i]).

inputs.description: Start index of the contiguous group (0-based, inclusive).

inputs.name: j
inputs.description: End index of the contiguous group (0-based, inclusive).

functions.name: solve
functions.description: Compute the minimum total sum of squared errors using the contiguous group partitioning DP. dp[g][i] represents the minimum SSE achievable using exactly g representative values to cover the first i distinct red values (sorted). Base case: dp[1][i] = cost(0, i-1). Transition: dp[g][i] = min over m in [g-1, i-1] of (dp[g-1][m] + cost(m, i-1)). If k >= d, every distinct value can be its own representative, so the answer is 0. Returns dp[min(k, d)][d].

structured_side_effects.description: Reads the entire test case from standard input via parse_input.
Prints exactly one integer (the minimum SSE) followed by a newline to standard output.

invariants: All functions use Python native integers; no floating-point arithmetic is used in final cost computation (weighted mean is computed as integer division for floor, +1 for ceil).
The values list is always sorted in strictly increasing order of r throughout all processing.
Allowed representative values range over all integers in [0, 255], not just input red values.
Optimal assignment of input values to nearest representative always yields contiguous clusters in sorted order, so the contiguous partitioning DP is exact.
No external dependencies; only Python 3.10+ standard library is used.
Prefix sum arrays s0, s1, s2 are computed once and shared immutably across all cost() and solve() calls.
The cost function evaluates at most two candidate representatives (floor and ceil of weighted mean), which is sufficient for optimality since the SSE as a function of integer v is convex.
k >= d implies the answer is 0 because each distinct value can be its own representative.

engineering_decisions.decision: Allowed values are any integer in [0,255], not restricted to input values
engineering_decisions.rationale: The problem says 'at most k integers from this range [0..255]'. Sample 3 confirms this: with values {0,25,50,255} and k=2, the optimal representatives are not from the input set (e.g., ~12 or 13 and 255), yielding SSE=37500000.
When values are sorted and each pixel maps to its nearest representative, optimal clusters are always contiguous intervals. This allows a standard interval DP approach.

engineering_decisions.decision: For each contiguous group, check floor and ceil of weighted mean as candidate representative
engineering_decisions.rationale: The optimal real-valued representative is the weighted mean. Since we need an integer, the best integer representative is either floor or ceil of the mean. We compute both and pick the one with lower cost.

The problem is a self-contained competitive programming problem solvable with ~100-200 lines of Python. All logic (parsing, precomputation, DP, output) shares the same data and is naturally implemented together.
